bullets.title: CRWV: Consensus bullish post Q3 beat — capacity sold out, pricing +35%, self-funding path
bullets.body: CoreWeave reported Q3 revenue of $3.66B (+168% YoY), 300bps above consensus, with non-GAAP operating margins of 10.4% vs. 6.9% expected; FY26 guidance raised with operating income midpoint +26% to $1.325B. Capacity effectively sold out through 2027 with 10x qualified demand vs. available supply; GPU pricing up ~35% QoQ with short-duration contracts >$40M/MW and 4-5yr deals at $20-25M/MW. Financing fears eased: $9B in customer prepayments, no unsecured debt needed through 2027; PTs range from $68 (Mizuho Neutral) to $149 (Citi Buy), with Oppenheimer at $150 and JPM/Piper tactically bullish. 2027 renewals could add ~$10B incremental annualized revenue with no additional capex.

bullets.title: NVDA: Baird downgrades to Neutral, cuts PT to $200; stock rebounds +3.5-5% pre-market
bullets.body: Baird downgraded NVDA to Neutral from Outperform and slashed its PT to $200 from $500 citing CEO Jensen Huang's spy scandal fallout and political pressure for resignation; Citi cut PT 10% to $285 on CEO sustainability risk and lower market multiples but maintained its Buy. Despite the downgrade, NVDA traded +3.5-5% pre-market as CRWV's AI infrastructure beat revived sector sentiment — NVDA's RSI hit 24, lowest since 2019. Morgan Stanley dropped NVDA from Top Pick under stop-loss but left OW rating intact; governance/China chip scrutiny remains the key overhang ahead of Nov. 17 earnings (consensus $2.47 EPS, $108.8B revenue).

bullets.title: GLW: Jefferies initiates Buy at $134 PT on AI-driven fiber shortage
bullets.body: Jefferies initiated Corning (GLW) with a Buy rating and $134 price target (20% upside from $112.13), calling it one of the clearest AI infrastructure beneficiaries with fiber demand running ahead of supply and multi-year hyperscaler agreements providing strong visibility. Photonics is cited as the next major opportunity, with optical scale-up expected to move fiber inside the box from 2028. The stock was up pre-market on the initiation alongside broad AI infrastructure strength.

bullets.title: TSM: October revenue +60% YoY tracking mid-to-high end of Q4 guidance; 'insatiable' demand
bullets.body: TSMC reported October revenue of NT$586.9bn (+60% YoY, +15% MoM), tracking to ~34% of Q4 consensus and pointing to the mid-to-high end of its guidance range. Gross margins expected flat QoQ at ~66.5%. JPM notes TSMC is accelerating capacity 2-3x typical annual build with four new N3 fabs and a steep N2 ramp; capex expected to reach $90B/$109B in 2027/28 with USD revenue growth of 40%/28% YoY. Management described leading-edge chip demand as 'insatiable.'

bullets.title: NVDA governance risk: CEO Huang under political fire; chip order cuts being considered
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag mounting governance risk around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — a senior GOP Senate Banking member called for his resignation over alleged China spy links, and the Commerce Department reportedly delayed placing a Nvidia-linked entity on a trade blacklist. Reports suggest Nvidia is considering chip order cuts amid export scrutiny. The US is also expected to close the 'neocloud loophole' blocking Chinese AI companies from accessing advanced Nvidia GPUs through third-country clouds.

bullets.title: Semis broadly rallying: SOX +5%, AMD +7%, AVGO +4.5%; DeMark buy signals accumulating
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOXX) surged ~5% pre-market on CRWV's AI infrastructure beat and renewed confidence in data center spending. AMD gained +7%, AVGO +4.5%, INTC +6%; memory names (MU, SNDK, STX, WDC) up 6-8% after being down 20-25% over the prior 10 days. UBS notes 70% of SOX constituents are near DeMark buy signals vs. 36.67% last week, the strongest technical setup in recent months.

bullets.title: VRT: JPMorgan initiates Neutral; stock +6.5% on AI/datacenter exposure
bullets.body: JPMorgan initiated Vertiv (VRT) at Neutral pre-market, while Mizuho highlighted VRT alongside ETN and HUBB as best-positioned in power for data center complexity tailwinds. Despite the Neutral initiation, VRT surged +6.5% pre-market reflecting broad AI infrastructure enthusiasm.

bullets.title: ADBE: Remains a frustration play; Neutral, $260-$315 PT range across brokers
bullets.body: Klein maintains Neutral on ADBE with a $260 PT, noting organic revenue/ARR growth anchored in high-single digits with no near-term catalyst. RBC maintains Outperform at $315 PT following Adobe Max, which showed strong focus on agentic software. Piper's enterprise software survey showed ADBE saw deceleration in pre-packaged AI adoption, though AI displacement of incumbent functionality ticked up.

bullets.title: T (AT&T): JPM reiterates OW at $31 PT; SpaceX not imminent threat, fiber/FWA strategy intact
bullets.body: AT&T management conveyed confidence in its converged fiber-mobile strategy; CEO Stankey estimated SpaceX wireless would be a 5th competitor requiring 2+ years to build scaled infrastructure. AT&T's D2D satellite service with AST SpaceMobile launches mid-2027. FWA expected to peak industry-wide late 2028 then decline with fiber at $35/300Mbps seen as superior. JPM reiterates OW with $31 PT; AT&T targets +3-4% EBITDA growth through 2027, +5% in 2028, with $45B+ capital returns.

bullets.title: WIX: PT cuts across brokers on FCF reduction; Base44 ARR at $250M growing but core decelerating
bullets.body: UBS cut WIX PT to $68 from $75 (Neutral) and RBC cut to $58 from $60; both cite reduced FY26 FCF margin guidance to ~16% from high-teens due to aggressive Base44 marketing and a ~$10M Q4 GPU prepayment headwind. Base44 ARR has grown rapidly to ~$250M from $150M in May but core self-creator business is flattish. First quarterly cohort's 12-month retention exceeded expectations; non-GAAP GM reached 58% in Q3, expected to approach core Wix levels (~70%) in 2027.

bullets.title: LYV: GS raises PT to $210, Roth reiterates Buy at $208; investor day highlights $1.875B AOI opportunity
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised Live Nation's incremental AOI opportunity to $1.875B (from $1.66B), implying ~11% annualized growth to $4.48B, and lifted its PT to $210. Concerts AOI per fan rising to $6+ from ~$4.30-4.40 in 2026; early 2027 demand up +8% YoY on shows and tickets. Roth reiterates Buy at $208 PT, citing a long-term double-digit AOI growth trajectory. Venue Nation opportunity increased to $925M with 38 large venue openings through 2031 at 20%+ IRRs.

bullets.title: GOOGL/META/AMZN: Agentic commerce inflecting in 2027; all three well-positioned
bullets.body: Citi sees agentic commerce at an inflection point with AI-driven retail traffic expected to grow 130% YoY this holiday vs. +4% for traditional search. AMZN's 400M+ Alexa Shopping users give it a data moat; META's Muse (4.4M global DAUs) is scaling social commerce; GOOGL's AI Mode prompts are 3x longer than traditional search, generating richer intent signals. AI-referred shoppers convert ~48% better than other traffic sources; consumer data depth — not model quality — expected to determine the winner.

bullets.title: INTU: Piper sees favorable FQ1 setup on Nov. 19; FY27 guidance embeds conservatism
bullets.body: Piper's morning call flagged a favorable setup for Intuit's FQ1 earnings on November 19, noting conservatism in FY27 guidance that could embed meaningful upside potential. No PT change mentioned.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings preview: implied move ±7.7% on Nov. 17; bearish options positioning at multi-year extreme
bullets.body: NVDA is down 29% since its Oct. 6 peak with net crowding at 3-year lows and put-call skew at the 89th percentile — the highest implied move (±7.7%) ahead of earnings since Feb 2025. Consensus expects $2.47 EPS and $108.8B in revenue. Citi expects a modest beat with 71.5% gross margin vs. the 72.1% consensus, partly offset by HBM price increases; FY28E revenue outlook of +70% YoY growth maintained.

bullets.title: CSCO/DIS: Upcoming earnings this week — CSCO Thu after close, DIS Nov. 17
bullets.body: Cisco reports Thursday after close (consensus $1.33 EPS, $18.12B revenue) and Disney reports November 17 before the open (consensus $1.69 EPS, $25.19B revenue). No pre-earnings research calls flagged beyond the earnings calendar.

bullets.title: NBIS: Reports Thursday before open; consensus ($0.71) EPS, $904.8M revenue
bullets.body: Nebius Group (NBIS) reports Thursday November 12 before market open with consensus EPS of ($0.71) and revenue of $904.8M. Wolfe's SaaS daily included an NBIS earnings preview; no specific directional view disclosed.

bullets.title: RCL: GS constructive following management meetings; 2027 upside from Caribbean capacity moderation
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs remains constructive on Royal Caribbean following a meeting that highlighted healthy consumer demand and onboard spending. 2027 upside seen from moderating Caribbean capacity growth and strong European demand.

bullets.title: PANW: Citi reiterates Buy at $440 PT; F1Q27 decent but elevated valuation limits asymmetry
bullets.body: Citi reaffirms Palo Alto Networks at Buy with a $440 PT but notes the stock trades at 16x EV/Sales '27 and ~42x EV/FCF '27 (up ~80% YTD), limiting near-term upside without a FY NGS ARR guidance raise. Constructive field signals include reinvigorated US public sector activity and a $2B TCV pipeline from Frontier AI Defense services; a topline beat quality and NGS ARR raise are the most sensitive inputs for a positive post-earnings reaction.

bullets.title: W (Wayfair): MS sees next leg in discretionary retail; W gaining share with category recovery optionality
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley identifies Wayfair as one of the key retail names for the next leg of the rotation, noting W is gaining share in a difficult market and a category recovery could drive a significant top-line kicker. Discretionary median NTM P/E has risen to 18x from 16x but remains below the 21x YE2025 level, requiring earnings follow-through in 2H27/2028. Earnings recovery potential and multiple expansion room cited.

bullets.title: PLTR: Mentioned in context of AIG DIY insurance platform challenging GWRE's positioning
bullets.body: Jefferies flagged that Guidewire faces an AI threat to its platform positioning in insurance from DIY approaches such as the AIG/PLTR partnership, potentially pressuring GWRE's upsell motion. No specific PT or rating change on PLTR itself.
